subject.title: [Bug]: Bootstrap files in agentDir are silently ignored — only workspace directory files are injected into system prompt

question: Should OpenClaw keep bootstrap prompt authority limited to workspace files and warn on bootstrap-named files in agentDir, or should explicitly configured agentDir files merge with or override workspace bootstrap files?
rationale: The source-level failure is clear, but the permanent fix changes a security-sensitive prompt authority boundary and three open closing PRs already implement different policies.

options.title: Warn and document workspace-only
options.body: Land a warning-only path, keep agentDir as state/auth storage, and make docs/diagnostics tell users to move prompt files into the workspace.

options.title: Adopt explicit agentDir bootstrap
options.body: Allow configured agentDir files to affect prompts, but require precedence docs, caller coverage, and upgrade/security proof before merge.

options.title: Defer for broader context design
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers decide the workspace, agentDir, and context-engine authority model together.

recommendation.title: Warn and document workspace-only
recommendation.body: Land a warning-only path, keep agentDir as state/auth storage, and make docs/diagnostics tell users to move prompt files into the workspace.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest bootstrap resolver history and is the safest owner for the prompt-authority boundary choice.
